title: Building TEEM with Claude: looking for feedback on free top-down action roguelite pre-alpha
author: vizyn
selftext:
I’m making TEEM, a top-down action roguelite where you steer thousands of insects around a glowing heart. You outnumber your enemy and mastering control of the swarm is the key to success.  This game was heavily inspired by Risk of Rain.

The free pre-alpha is available for Windows and Linux: [Download TEEM.](https://vizyn.itch.io/teem)

Development has primarily used Claude Opus 5.5 for codegen, Meshy-generated boss models and ElevenLabs-generated sound effects and music.  There is an opt-in for sharing your run data with me (and bug reports in the pause menu) which Claude monitors to create bots that mimic real player behavior and card up bugs.  Bot runs with various strategies have been my primary source of data for balance decisions since playtesters have been hard to come by at this point.

I’d appreciate a playtest of the current build so I have more player-driven data to model bots after for balance tuning.  I'd also appreciate honest feedback spanning:

- Is the core gameplay loop appealing?
- I'm aiming for a difficulty curve where a base difficulty run (no difficulty modifiers) is won through primarily game knowledge and forgiving of mechanical mistakes.. did I hit that mark?
- If you decided to give it a go but didn't enjoy it what were your issues with it?

Happy to playtest a game in return.
